claims.text: Conventional fixed-parameter, high-thermal-load laser additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces steep thermal gradients, high residual stresses, and degraded mechanical properties.
An integrated thermal-imaging and ML feedback loop can dynamically adjust laser power and scan behavior during an AlCrFeNiSi build.
The applicable feedback-control window is 200–400 W laser power and 600–1200 mm/s scan speed.
Dynamic control can maintain the peak local temperature below 700 °C during fabrication.
The proposed process applies to 5–10 mm cubes and miniature dog-bone specimens made with 30–40 µm layers in an inert, preheated environment.
Real-time thermal feedback will produce a more uniform thermal profile during solidification.
A more uniform thermal profile will refine and homogenize the microstructure.
Instant ML-driven changes to laser parameters will prevent excessive local heating.
Reducing steep thermal gradients reduces internal stresses and microstructural defects.
ML-controlled AlCrFeNiSi builds will have lower residual thermal stress than fixed-parameter high-thermal-load builds.
ML-controlled builds will exhibit less warpage than conventional fixed-parameter builds.
ML-controlled builds will exhibit higher yield strength and ductility than conventional fixed-parameter builds.
Improved tensile properties will result from a more controlled and homogeneous microstructure.
The intervention will be most effective within the stated power, speed, layer-thickness, and miniature-geometry window.
Effectiveness on larger or more complex geometries is uncertain.
Failure to achieve at least approximately 15% lower residual stress or approximately 10% higher yield strength or ductility would falsify the hypothesis.
